m: The armour of the Goddess. Now the armour of the Goddess. Om. Of this Shri Chandi armour, the seer is Brahma, the metre is anushtubh, and the deity is Chamunda. The seed is the mothers named in the limb-placement, and the element is the deities of the binding of the directions. This direction is for its recitation as a limb of the Saptashati, to please the Mother of the world. Om. Salutation to Chandika. Markandeya said: Om. Tell me, grandfather, that which is the supreme secret in the world, which makes every protection for human beings, and which has not been told to anyone.
Brahma said: There is a most secret thing, twice-born one, a benefit to all beings, the meritorious armour of the Goddess. Hear it, great sage.
The first is Shailaputri, the second Brahmacharini, the third Chandraghanta, and the fourth Kushmanda.
The fifth is Skandamata, the sixth Katyayani, the seventh Kalaratri, and the eighth Mahagauri.
The ninth is Siddhidatri. These are famed as the nine Durgas. These names were spoken by Brahma himself, the great one.
One who is being burned by fire, one who has gone into the midst of enemies in battle, and those pained by fear who have gone for refuge in a difficult and hard place —
nothing inauspicious arises for them in the danger of battle. I do not see a calamity for that person, nor grief, sorrow, or fear.
For those by whom you are remembered with devotion, increase surely arises. Those who remember you, sovereign of the gods, you protect. Of this there is no doubt.
Chamunda is established among the departed. Varahi is seated on a buffalo. Aindri is mounted on an elephant. Vaishnavi is seated on Garuda.
Maheshvari is mounted on a bull. Kaumari has a peacock as her mount. Lakshmi, the Goddess, is seated on a lotus, a lotus in her hand, dear to Hari.
The Goddess who bears a white form, the sovereign, has a bull as her mount. Brahmi is mounted on a swan and adorned with every ornament.
All these mothers are joined with every yoga, rich in the beauty of many ornaments, and adorned with many jewels.
The Goddesses are seen mounted on chariots, filled with anger, bearing conch, discus, mace, spear, plough, and the weapon that is a pestle,
a shield, a lance, an axe, a noose, a spear-weapon, a trident, and the excellent weapon that is the sharnga bow.
They bear weapons in this way for the destruction of the bodies of daityas, for the fearlessness of devotees, and indeed for the welfare of the gods.
Salutation to you, greatly fierce one, of greatly terrible prowess, of great strength, of great energy, destroyer of great fear.
Protect me, Goddess, hard to look upon, increaser of the fear of enemies. May Aindri guard me in the east, and the deity of fire in the southeast.
May Varahi protect me in the south, and the sword-bearer in the southwest. May Varuni guard me in the west, and she whose mount is a deer in the northwest.
May Kaumari protect me in the north, and the spear-bearer in the northeast. May Brahmani guard me above, and Vaishnavi below.
May Chamunda, whose mount is a corpse, guard the ten directions in this way. May Jaya protect me in front, and Vijaya behind.
Ajita on the left side, and Aparajita on the right. May Udyotini guard the crest, and Uma, established on the head.
May Maladhari guard the forehead, and Yashasvini the eyebrows. Trinetra between the brows, and Yamaghanta the nose.
Shankhini between the eyes, and she who dwells at the gates, at the ears. May Kalika guard the cheeks, and Shankari at the root of the ears.
Sugandha at the nose, and Charchika on the upper lip. Amritakala on the lower lip, and Sarasvati on the tongue.
May Kaumari guard the teeth, and Chandika at the throat. Chitraghanta the bell of the throat, and Mahamaya the palate.
May Kamakshi guard the chin, and Sarvamangala my speech. Bhadrakali at the neck, and the bow-bearer along the spine.
Nilagriva on the outside of the throat, and Nalakubari the windpipe. May the sword-bearer guard the two shoulders, and the thunderbolt-bearer my arms.
May Dandini guard the two hands, and Ambika the fingers. May Shuleshvari guard the nails, and Kuleshvari the belly.
May Mahadevi, destroyer of the mind's grief, guard the breasts. Lalita the Goddess at the heart, and the spear-bearer in the stomach.
May Kamini guard the navel, and Guhyeshvari the private part. Putana and Kamika the organ, and she whose mount is a buffalo the seat.
May the blessed one guard the hips, and she who dwells in the Vindhyas the two knees. May Mahabala, giver of every desire, guard the shanks.
Narasimhi at the two ankles, and Taijasi on the back of the feet. May Shri guard the toes, she who dwells on the soles of the feet.
Damshtrakarali the nails, and she of upward-standing hair the hair. Kuberi in the pores, and Vagishvari the skin.
Parvati the blood, marrow, fat, flesh, bone, and marrow-fat. Kalaratri the intestines, and Mukuteshvari the bile.
Padmavati in the lotus of the heart, and Chudamani the phlegm. Jvalamukhi the flame of the nails, unpierceable in all the joints.
May Brahmani guard my seed, and Chatreshvari the shadow. May Dharmadharini guard my I-sense, mind, and understanding.
And the prana, apana, vyana, udana, and samana breaths. May she of the thunderbolt hand guard them, and Kalyana-shobhana my life.
Yogini in taste, form, scent, sound, and touch. May Narayani always guard sattva, rajas, and tamas.
May Varahi guard life, and Vaishnavi dharma. May the discus-bearer guard fame, glory, Lakshmi, wealth, and learning.
May Indrani guard my family line. Guard my cattle, Chandika. May Mahalakshmi guard the sons, and Bhairavi the wife.
May Supatha guard the road, and likewise Kshemakari the way. Mahalakshmi at the king's door, and Vijaya standing on every side.
Whatever place is left without a guard, left out by the armour, guard all of that for me, Goddess Jayanti, destroyer of sin.
One should not go a single step if one desires one's own good, unless always wrapped in the armour, wherever one goes.

There, in each place, there is gain of wealth and victory that fulfills every wish. Whatever desire one thinks, that one certainly obtains. A person will obtain unequalled supreme sovereignty on earth.
A mortal becomes fearless, unconquered in battles. Wrapped in the armour, a person would be worthy of worship in the three worlds.
This armour of the Goddess is hard for even the gods to obtain. Whoever recites it every day, restrained, at the three junctures, joined with faith,
a divine art would be his, and he is unconquered in the three worlds. He would live a hundred years and more, free of untimely death.
All diseases perish, beginning with those of the spider and of eruption. Whatever poison is plant, moving, or even prepared,
and all hostile rites, mantras, and yantras on earth, those who move on the earth, those who move in the sky, those born in water, and those who instruct,
the inborn, the family-born, the garland, the dakini and the shakini, and the dreadful dakinis of great strength who move in the atmosphere,
seizing planets, ghosts, and pishachas, yakshas, gandharvas, and rakshasas, brahma-rakshasas, vetalas, kushmandas, bhairavas, and the rest —
they perish at the sight of the person in whose heart the armour is established. Honour and elevation would come from kings. It is the supreme maker of an increase of splendour.
He also grows by renown, adorned with glory on earth. One should recite the Saptashati, Chandi, having first made the armour.
As long as the circle of the earth endures, with its mountains, woods, and forests, so long a lineage of sons and grandsons remains on earth.
At the end of the body, a person always obtains the supreme place, which is hard for even the gods to obtain, by the grace of Mahamaya.
He obtains the supreme form and rejoices with Shiva. Om.
